The Log-Jacobian of a Separable Penalty's Map

Source: R/distrib_penalty.R
dp_log_jacobian.Rd

Returns \(\log\lvert\det D\rvert\) for the map \(D\) of a separable penalty: 0 when the penalty has no map, the sum of the logarithms of the absolute diagonal entries for a diagonal map, and the stored log_jacobian property for any other map.

Usage

dp_log_jacobian(penalty)

Arguments

penalty

A DistribPenalty() object.

Value

A single number, possibly NA.

Details

For a diagonal map the quantity is recomputed from the entries, at the cost of \(q\) logarithms, so that the result stays correct when a caller replaces the map with a subset of its diagonal through S7::set_props() and the stored property is out of date. A diagonal map with a zero or missing entry gives NA, as does a stored property that is NA because the map is not square or is singular.

See also

distrib_penalty()

Examples

d <- distributions7::fixed(distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), mu = 0)
pen <- distrib_penalty(d, n_coef = 3)
dp_log_jacobian(pen)
#> [1] 0
pen2 <- distrib_penalty(d, map = Matrix::Diagonal(x = c(1, 2, 4)))
all.equal(dp_log_jacobian(pen2), log(8))
#> [1] TRUE
